title: Indus Operational Mathematics: A Formal Framework for State-Based Symbol Systems
description: This repository presents a formal mathematical framework for analyzing the Indus Valley (Harappan) script through operational mathematics and state-based computation. The framework includes: (1) A formal axiomatic system with five core axioms, (2) Comparative analysis with ancient Chinese character transformations, (3) Formal verification in Lean 4, Coq, Isabelle/HOL, and Agda, (4) Python and C++ implementations, (5) A comprehensive LaTeX monograph. Key contribution: We demonstrate that both Harappan and ancient Chinese writing systems share operational logic where graphical modifications represent state transformations. The TCOP (Total Closure of Operations Principle) theorem formally captures this insight. NON-CLAIMS: This work does NOT claim to decipher the Indus script phonetically, provide linguistic translations, or establish historical meanings of symbols.
references: Farmer, S., Sproat, R., & Witzel, M. (2004). The Collapse of the Indus-Script Thesis: The Myth of a Literate Harappan Civilization.
Rao, R. P. N., et al. (2009). Entropic Evidence for Linguistic Structure in the Indus Script. Science, 324(5931), 1165-1165.
Pierce, B. C. (2002). Types and Programming Languages. MIT Press.
Plotkin, G. D. (2004). A Structural Approach to Operational Semantics. Journal of Logic and Algebraic Programming, 60, 17-139.
